I will keep my farm centered on the wheat-maize system, because I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain and that rotation matches my climate, irrigation conditions, machinery, and market stability. I value output, risk control, and operational efficiency more than chasing a niche crop, so I will put most of my land into winter wheat followed by summer maize. I will keep a smaller block in spring peanut to spread risk, reduce continuous cereal pressure on part of the land, and give myself some cash-flow flexibility. Because I am well educated, I will lean on improved or hybrid seed, measured fertilizer use, and tighter field management instead of broad, wasteful input use.

For management, I will use ploughing before wheat where I want better residue incorporation and root development, then rotary tillage for maize and peanut to move quickly after harvest or before sowing. I will not over-irrigate; in my area groundwater matters, so I will irrigate wheat at the key stages, give maize a few timely irrigations in hot periods, and keep peanut lighter. I will apply nitrogen more heavily to maize and wheat, keep phosphorus steady for root establishment, and maintain potassium especially for maize and peanut. I will not spray on a calendar just to spray; I will keep pesticide applications moderate and tied to weed, aphid, rust, armyworm, and disease pressure. My goal is a stable, high-probability year rather than the absolute highest possible yield.
